solution: Equidistance from \((-2,3)\), \((6,-1)\) and \((4,3)\) gives the perpendicular bisectors \(2h-k=3\) (of the first two vertices) and \(h-2k=3\) (of the last two). Solving: \(h=1,\,k=-1\). Circumcentre \(= (1,-1)\). Matches option D.
note: second bisector was written h - 2k = -3 (that system solves to (3, 3)); it is h - 2k = 3. Key D unchanged.

solution: Centre on Y-axis: \((0,a)\). Equal distances: \(16+a^2=(a-2)^2\Rightarrow 16=-4a+4 \Rightarrow a=-3\). \(r=\sqrt{16+9}=5\). \(r^2-r+1=25-5+1=21\). Matches option B.
note: a stray +4 in the distance equation gave a = 3; it is a = -3. Radius 5 and key B unchanged.

solution: Let \(PQ = p\) and \(RS = q\). Since \(X\) lies on the circle and \(PR\) is a diameter, \(\angle PXR = 90^\circ\), so \(PS \perp RQ\). The tangents at \(P\) and \(R\) are perpendicular to \(PR\), so triangle \(QPR\) is right-angled at \(P\) and triangle \(PRS\) at \(R\). Then \(\angle PRQ = 90^\circ - \angle RPS = \angle PSR\), so triangles \(QPR\) and \(PRS\) are similar and \(\dfrac{PQ}{PR} = \dfrac{PR}{RS}\). Hence \(PR^2 = PQ\cdot RS\), and since \(PR = 2r\), \(2r = \sqrt{pq} = \sqrt{PQ\cdot RS}\). Matches option A.
note: the XP*XR = chord^2 step is not an identity and the result was asserted; replaced with the similar-triangles proof (PR^2 = PQ*RS). Key A unchanged.
